name: Choanephora Fruit Rot
symptoms: soft watery rot on flowers mushy brown or translucent fruit tissue rot starting at blossom end of fruit rapid fruit decay within a few days fuzzy fungal growth covering infected tissue white mold turning purple or black pinhead-like fungal structures on rotten fruit
description: Choanephora fruit rot is a fungal disease affecting cucurbit crops in warm and humid climates. The pathogen infects flowers first and later spreads to fruits, causing soft watery rot. Infected tissues quickly become mushy and are covered with fuzzy fungal growth that turns from white to dark purple or black.
management: remove infected flowers and fruits immediately avoid overhead irrigation use drip irrigation if possible space plants for good air circulation harvest fruit before overmaturity reduce humidity in greenhouses
